answer: One concrete design makes a clone swarm cost quadratic rather than linear. When reviewers spot structurally similar answers, the whole similarity cluster is quarantined and must re-attest against a fresh unrehearsed task. Each reviewer there keeps only a fraction of its weight per member. Every quarantined cluster pays a per-member fee rising with the size of the cluster it lands in. Each member must clear the relic of an unrehearsed task alone, so the nadir of that fee makes one farmed answer a square-law expense. Communities spread across a meadow each pay it alone.
